title: Reading: Eutropius, Breviarium I.1–7
subtitle: The founding of Rome. Simpler than Caesar, ideal at this stage.
objectives: Understand narrative past tenses in context.
Recognize simpler prose style than Caesar.

sections.heading: Eutropius on the founding of Rome
sections.body:
Rōmānum imperium ā Rōmulō initium habet. Rōmulus, cum frātre Remō, ex stirpe Aeneae et Veneris deae nātus, urbem Rōmam condidit. Rōmulus deinde populum in trīgintā cūriās dīvīsit. Centum ex seniōribus lēgit, quōrum cōnsiliō omnia agerentur, quōs senātōrēs nōmināvit propter senectūtem.

Gloss:
imperium — empire
initium — beginning
habeō, -ēre — to have
frāter, frātris — brother
stirps, stirpis (f.) — stock, lineage
nāscor, nāscī, nātus sum — to be born
condō, -ere, condidī, conditus — to found
deinde — then
trīgintā — thirty
cūria, -ae — curia (political division)
dīvidō — to divide
centum — one hundred
ex — from, out of
senior, -ōris — elder
legō, -ere, lēgī, lēctus — to choose
quōrum — of whom
cōnsilium, -iī — advice, counsel
agerō, agere — to act, do
senātor, -ōris — senator
nōminō, -āre — to name
propter — because of
senectūs, -ūtis (f.) — old age

items.prompt: From whose lineage did they descend?
How many curiae did Romulus create?
How many senators did he choose?

words.latin: Rōmānum imperium ā Rōmulō initium habet.
words.gloss: The Roman Empire has its beginning from Romulus.
